svg.text: IR Platform — the HashiCorp zero-trust layer, implemented

Four products, four controls, one composed path. Each card states what the product enforces in this deployment and the UAT that proves it. The component wiring is in architecture.svg; the generated structure is CODE_GRAPH.md.
Boundary — session-aware ingress
the analyst hop is an authenticated, authorized, auditable session — not a forwarder
Authority in the enclave
controller · database · grants · encryption roots
recovery key never leaves the tier · the DMZ runs
a session CLIENT and holds no authority
One target
the SSO gate, per session, per principal — every
other service has no target and no route · egress
worker in the enclave is the only DMZ-facing proxy
Supervised session
controller rebuilt, worker recreated, expiry, proxy
error — the client re-authenticates and re-establishes
unattended; a canceled session is replaced by a
NEW authorized one, never a lingering socket
Truthful access record
Brokered Sessions page = who, from where, to what,
how long, how much, why ended · abandoned sessions
are canceled, so "active" means active · the page's
credential can list and read — a cancel is REFUSED
PROVEN: test/uat_boundary.sh — placement · no authority in the DMZ · one target · attribution ·
traffic end to end · healing · the record matches the controller's own, read via a second authority
tailnet transport: headscale below · session data path: Boundary per-session mutual TLS
browser symptom of the down window is PR_END_OF_FILE_ERROR — the listener heals in seconds
Consul — the service mesh that enforces
a compromised container must not reach the evidence just because it shares a network
Sidecars are the only listeners
Postgres and MinIO bind 127.0.0.1 ONLY — every
connection terminates at a Connect proxy: mutual
TLS, then an intention check, on every connection
Intentions — default-deny, converged
policy in hashicorp/consul/config-entries/, written
to Consul on EVERY deploy — bootstrap entries never
update an existing cluster · UI shows the enforced matrix
Hardened control plane
TLS on every port, cleartext disabled · gossip
encrypted · ACLs default-deny · per-service tokens:
no service can edit the intention that governs it
read-only token for the UI's mesh page
Namespace convergence · multi-host
a recreated service strands its proxy in a dead netns —
deploy compares namespace inodes and repairs; the
mesh-reattach repair does it on demand · per-host
sidecar listeners via IR_MESH_ADDR_* / IR_MESH_PORT_*
PROVEN: test/uat_consul.sh — 49 assertions: cleartext closed · uncertified refused · untokened denied ·
denied pairs refused ON THE WIRE · allowed pairs carry traffic · per-sidecar namespace-inode match
open item, stated in SECURITY-MODEL.md: podman-compose → pods/quadlets migration
Vault — secrets with a lifecycle
no static credential worth stealing sits in a file the application tier reads
Dynamic database users
minted against a stable owning role (objects never
orphan) · delivered by Vault Agent render, read at
start · reconciled on every deploy, sealed or not
reached THROUGH the mesh, like any other client
Rotation and break-glass
rotate-app-creds.sh revokes, re-issues, restarts the
app tier in order (services, then their sidecars) ·
break-glass mints a temporary root from the unseal
key and revokes it after use · KV holds custody HMAC
PROVEN: test/uat_vault.sh — 23 assertions, including a live credential minted through the mesh
sealed by design after restart — the Unseal Vault repair (or deploy.sh enclave) brings it back;
every credential the application tier needs is unavailable until then, and that is the point
provisioning uses a bounded ir-provisioner AppRole — the root token is never stored
headscale — the analyst transport · and the one privileged executor
WireGuard to exactly one port; repairs by name, never by command
Tailnet, deny-by-default
workstations enroll against a pinned control plane ·
DERP relay over TLS · no subnet routes advertised —
"cannot address an internal host" is a routing fact ·
the bastion distributes across N sessions; a broker, not a router
Remediation agent (ir-agent)
network NONE · pid host · runtime socket only · its own
compose project, so no repair can recreate its executor ·
admin requests a NAME; the agent's own allow-list
decides what that means · outcomes final, audited
PROVEN: test/uat_tailnet.sh — the tunnel carries the session and bounds it (no internal reach)
test/uat_repairs.sh — 18 assertions: posture, refusals, the loop, a repair that repairs, finality
all six repairs also executed from the UI — each recorded succeeded with output and exit code
THE COMPOSED PATH
workstation ──WireGuard──▶ bastion listener ──Boundary session (per-session mTLS)──▶ egress worker ──▶ Traefik + oauth2-proxy ──OIDC──▶ Keycloak ──▶ app
app / worker / puller ──sidecar mTLS + intention──▶ Postgres · MinIO
Vault ──through the mesh──▶ dynamic credentials for all of them
admin (UI) ──named request──▶ queue ──claimed──▶ remediation agent ──allow-list──▶ podman / deploy scripts
every hop above: TLS, attributable, tested
Capstone:
test/uat_e2e.sh — 32 assertions: collect → ship → pull → analyze → enforce → audit → carve → stage → reverse engineer, on both GUI workstations
Model:
SECURITY-MODEL.md P1–P10 — each principle names its enforcement and its proof
